correctness.rationale: For every connected cactus, graph incidence zonotope volume equals sqrt(N) times its spanning tree count. Every graph-cut facet has area sqrt(st) tau(G[S]) tau(G[T]) and height k sqrt(N/st)/2, giving normalized mass k tau(G[S])tau(G[T])/(2d tau(G)). Cactus bond classification leaves exactly one bridge edge or two same-cycle edges. Deleting them preserves all cycles or removes precisely one cycle, yielding respectively 1/(2d) and 1/(d ell). Counts and sum-one are exact. If-and-only-if equal masses follows from ell>=3 and equality across lengths. Exact integer cut/Gram checks and convex-hull validation confirm finite examples; code cannot prove the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The precise Euclidean cone-volume distribution of a canonical infinite graph-zonotope family is a natural Minkowski-type metric invariant. The sharp uniform-mass iff theorem distinguishes nonparallelotope bridgeless equal-cycle cacti from mixed and unequal-cycle cacti even though all are built from simple blocks. Aggregate block weights are topology-independent and give a general geometric conservation law. This is not a mere known facet count or isolated numerical computation.
